headline: Apple & Intel strike US chip manufacturing deal, Trump claims
summary: Donald Trump asserts Apple has finalized a partnership with Intel to design and manufacture chips domestically, though neither company has confirmed.
details: Donald Trump has claimed on Truth Social that Apple has reached a definitive agreement with Intel for chip design and manufacturing within the United States. This announcement follows previous reports from May suggesting a preliminary deal between the two tech giants.

While neither Apple nor Intel has officially confirmed the alleged partnership, reports indicate that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick played a key role in facilitating discussions. The aim was to revive the relationship between Apple and Intel, which previously collaborated before Apple shifted to its own silicon, largely produced by TSMC.

Renowned Apple analyst Ming-Chi Kuo had previously reported that Intel would begin testing production for Apple processors on its 18A-P process throughout 2026, with actual production and delivery slated for the following year. Intel is expected to produce chips for Apple's iPhones and Macs at its facilities in Oregon, Arizona, and Ohio.

Despite this potential collaboration, TSMC is anticipated to continue handling the majority of Apple's chip manufacturing. Trump also mentioned that the US government took a 10% stake in Intel, which was partly funded by the CHIPS Act and the Secure Enclave program.
caption:
Donald Trump claims Apple and Intel have finalized a deal for US chip manufacturing, but neither company has confirmed.

Donald Trump has claimed on Truth Social that Apple has reached a definitive agreement with Intel for chip design and manufacturing within the United States. This announcement follows previous reports from May suggesting a preliminary deal between the two tech giants.

While neither Apple nor Intel has officially confirmed the alleged partnership, reports indicate that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick played a key role in facilitating discussions. The aim was to revive the relationship between Apple and Intel, which previously collaborated before Apple shifted to its own silicon, largely produced by TSMC.

Renowned Apple analyst Ming-Chi Kuo had previously reported that Intel would begin testing production for Apple processors on its 18A-P process throughout 2026, with actual production and delivery slated for the following year. Intel is expected to produce chips for Apple's iPhones and Macs at its facilities in Oregon, Arizona, and Ohio.

Despite this potential collaboration, TSMC is anticipated to continue handling the majority of Apple's chip manufacturing. Trump also mentioned that the US government took a 10% stake in Intel, which was partly funded by the CHIPS Act and the Secure Enclave program.
